title: A Demonstration of Correlation Analysis in Python and Quarto
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import seaborn as sns 

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

The members of Insect Habitat Builders Club have been struggling with finding real estate for their insect terrariums for many years now. A new flower has started becoming more popular, and they want to see if the width of a flower petal is correlated to the length. Measurements of petals of flowers of different species were taken to test this, totalling 150 samples.


Literature Review


Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters), we will evaluate this relationship using a simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these.


Results

corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > 0.8: 
    narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0.4:
    narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
    narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -0.4:
    narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"

Using the classic simple Pearson correlation appraoch these data produce a correlation coefficient of 0.96287, as such, given this result we conclude that the relationship is a very strong positive correlation.

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize = (6,3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data = df, y = 'petal_length', x = 'petal_width')
 
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (mm)')







Figure 1: A scatterplot of petal length and width





As shown in Figure 1, we see additional evidence of a strong positive correlation between an iris flower petal length and petal width.


Discussion
Now that this long-standing probelm is resolved thanks to the dilligent efforts of the Club, science has once again triumphed in establishing that there is a positive correlative relationship between Iris petal length and Iris petal width as a matter of empirically cetain round truth.

sns.lmplot(data = df, y = 'petal_length', x = 'petal_width')







Figure 2: A linear model plot of petal length and width
